summary: Vectors describe forces, velocities and positions. You derive what the dot product and the cross product mean geometrically, compute the moment a force makes about a joint, and implement dot, cross and norm without calling a library.
html:
Vectors as arrows and as lists

A vector in 3D is a list of three numbers a=(ax​,ay​,az​) measured along fixed axes. It is also an arrow with a length ∥a∥=ax2​+ay2​+az2​​ and a direction. You will switch between these two views all the time: the list is what code stores, the arrow is what you reason about.

The dot product measures alignment

Define the dot product algebraically as

a⋅b=ax​bx​+ay​by​+az​bz​.

To see what it means, apply the law of cosines to the triangle with sides a, b and a−b:

∥a−b∥2=∥a∥2+∥b∥2−2∥a∥∥b∥cosθ.

Expanding the left side with the algebraic definition gives ∥a∥2+∥b∥2−2a⋅b. Comparing the two,

a⋅b=∥a∥∥b∥cosθ.

So the dot product is zero for perpendicular vectors, positive when they point the same way, and a⋅u^ is the length of a’s shadow on a unit direction u^. Mechanical work W=F⋅d is exactly that shadow: only the part of the force along the motion does work.

The cross product is an area with a direction

The cross product of two 3D vectors is

a×b=​ay​bz​−az​by​az​bx​−ax​bz​ax​by​−ay​bx​​​.

Three facts follow from the formula, and you can check each by expanding it:

  • a⋅(a×b)=0 and b⋅(a×b)=0, so the result is perpendicular to both inputs.
  • ∥a×b∥=∥a∥∥b∥sinθ, the area of the parallelogram the two vectors span.
  • b×a=−a×b. Order matters; the direction follows the right-hand rule.

Moments about a joint

A force F applied at a point r from a joint creates the moment (torque)

M=r×F.

Its direction is the axis the force tries to turn the body about, and its size is the force times the perpendicular lever arm. This one line is the basis of statics, robot joint torques and the rotational dynamics of Phase 03.

Worked example: torque on a gripper joint

A gripper pad sits at r=(0.2, 0.1, 0) m from the wrist joint and carries a load of F=(0, 0, −50) N (about 5 kg hanging).

M=​0.1⋅(−50)−0⋅00⋅0−0.2⋅(−50)0.2⋅0−0.1⋅0​​=​−5100​​ N⋅m.

The size is 25+100​=11.18 N·m. Check perpendicularity: M⋅r=−1+1+0=0 and M⋅F=0. A wrist motor about the x axis feels 5 N·m; one about the y axis feels 10 N·m.

Code it from scratch

vec.py
import math, random
import numpy as np

def dot(a, b):
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b))

def norm(a):
    return math.sqrt(dot(a, a))

def cross(a, b):
    ax, ay, az = a
    bx, by, bz = b
    return (ay * bz - az * by, az * bx - ax * bz, ax * by - ay * bx)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    M = cross((0.2, 0.1, 0.0), (0.0, 0.0, -50.0))
    assert np.allclose(M, (-5, 10, 0)) and abs(norm(M) - 11.1803) < 1e-4
    rng = random.Random(0)
    for _ in range(1000):
        a = [rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(3)]
        b = [rng.uniform(-1, 1) for _ in range(3)]
        c = cross(a, b)
        assert np.allclose(c, np.cross(a, b), atol=1e-12)
        assert abs(dot(c, a)) < 1e-12 and abs(dot(c, b)) < 1e-12
        assert abs(dot(a, b) - np.dot(a, b)) < 1e-12
    print("dot, cross and norm match NumPy on 1000 random pairs")

Exercises

Find the angle between a=(1,2,3) and b=(4,−5,6).

Show the solution
  1. a⋅b=4−10+18=12.
  2. ∥a∥=14​=3.742, ∥b∥=77​=8.775.
  3. cosθ=12/(3.742×8.775)=0.3655, so θ=68.56°.

A 30 N force pushes along (0,1,0) at the end of a 0.4 m arm that points along (cos30°,sin30°,0). What torque does the joint at the origin feel?

Show the solution
  1. r=0.4(0.866,0.5,0)=(0.3464,0.2,0) m, F=(0,30,0) N.
  2. M=r×F=(0,0,0.3464×30−0.2×0)=(0,0,10.39) N·m.
  3. Only the force component perpendicular to the arm counts: 0.4×30cos30°=10.39 N·m.

quiz.q: What is ∥a×b∥ for the same two vectors?
quiz.explain: a×b=(27,6,−13) and 729+36+169​=934​=30.56.

quiz.q: The cross product r×F is always…
quiz.explain: Expanding r⋅(r×F) gives zero term by term, and the same for F. Swapping the order flips the sign.
options: perpendicular to both r and F
unchanged if you swap r and F

quiz.q: A 20 N force acts perpendicular to a 0.15 m lever. What is the size of the moment in N·m?
quiz.explain: ∥r∥∥F∥sin90°=0.15×20=3 N·m.

quiz.q: The dot product of a force with a displacement gives…
quiz.explain: Work is the component of force along the motion times the distance, W=F⋅d.
